text:
sam: Hey team, hi! First day on an M2 MacBook Pro. Trying to bootstrap dev environment. Using zsh. I cloned dotfiles into ~/dotfiles and ran the install script but my PATH order looks wrong: `which node` -> /usr/bin/node and `asdf list` shows nodejs 18.16.0 installed. asdf shims are in ~/.asdf/shims but not being picked up. Any quick zsh-specific tips? Also where do I put REDWOOD_API_KEY locally for quick prototyping?
dee: welcome sam :wave: quick things to check: 1) ensure ~/.asdf/shims is prepended to PATH before /usr/bin; on zsh put that in ~/.zprofile not ~/.zshrc for login shells. 2) add `source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh` or `eval "$(asdf init zsh)"` depending on your asdf version. 3) run `asdf reshim nodejs` after install.
ivan: fwiw our dotfiles installer usually symlinks files into ~ and drops a small ~/_envrc with direnv settings. If you use direnv, add REDWOOD_API_KEY to .envrc in the repo root or use a local .envrc with `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` and run `direnv allow`. We prefer direnv for ephemeral keys.
sam: thanks. My installer put asdf init in ~/.zshrc instead of ~/.zprofile. Moving it fixed path ordering. Node shows v18 now. For REDWOOD_API_KEY I only see a vault shortcut in 1Password but not sure which entry.
dee: 1Password -> Vaults -> Redwood -> Personal Dev Keys has entries named `redwood-alex-test` etc. If you need a personal dev key, ping infra or create a ticket in #support. For onboarding, use a short-lived key with limited scope.
onboard-bot: (bot) Hey sam! If you'd like a 1:1 setup pairing, reply with "book" and I'll DM a calendar to schedule with DevEx. Also see https://handbook.redwood.dev/onboarding/dev-setup for a checklist.
ivan: a couple extra mac quirks: - make sure homebrew is the arm64 path (/opt/homebrew). `brew --prefix` should return that. If it returns /usr/local you likely have x86 brew which can complicate ruby builds. - For building Ruby with asdf/ruby, set: `export LDFLAGS='-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib'` and `export CPPFLAGS='-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/include'` before `asdf install ruby <version>`.
sam: ran reshim and moved init, node is good. Ran into GPG pinentry when installing commit signing keys. Error: pinentry-curses not found.
dee: on mac install `pinentry-mac` via brew: `brew install pinentry-mac` then add to gpg-agent conf: `pinentry-program /opt/homebrew/bin/pinentry-mac` and `export GPG_TTY=$(tty)` in your shell. Restart gpg-agent with `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent` then `gpgconf --launch gpg-agent`.
ivan: if you use a security key (YubiKey) also install `gpg` and `scdaemon` and run `gpg --card-status`. We have a short doc in the handbook about yubikey pairing.
sam: sweet that fixed gpg. One last thing: docker-compose permissions error on Mac with docker desktop volumes. Any quick workaround?
dee: prefer using our devcontainer if you hit volume permission weirdness. Quick local fix: `sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) ~/projectdir` or run docker with our helper script `scripts/dev-docker.sh` which drops you into container with proper mounts.
ops: (ops) Also note we store cluster/service credentials in 1Password; never commit keys to dotfiles. For CI, we use Vault-backed secrets injected at runtime. If you need CI creds, open an infra ticket.
sam: mega helpful, thanks everyone! I'll follow up if anything else breaks. Book me for a pairing sesh later :slightly_smiling_face:
